content.value_statement: Inconsistent API contracts create integration errors and expensive migrations. This skill applies reusable REST, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenAPI, and AsyncAPI patterns to create clear contracts.
actual_capabilities: Compares REST, GraphQL, and gRPC approaches for different service requirements.
Defines REST naming, methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, versioning, and rate limiting patterns.
Provides GraphQL schema, query, mutation, pagination, and field-level error patterns.
Provides gRPC service, message, streaming, pagination, and status code examples.
Includes reusable OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI 3.0 specification templates.
Supplies a checklist for design, security, documentation, testing, deployment, and post-launch review.
limitations: Provides guidance and templates but does not implement or deploy API services.
Does not validate specifications with linters or test live endpoints.
Cannot select production authentication or authorization policies without system requirements.
Uses placeholder domains, data, and schemas that require project-specific adaptation.

use_cases.title: Design a new service contract
use_cases.description: Create consistent resources, operations, responses, errors, pagination, and authentication rules before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize team API conventions
use_cases.description: Establish shared REST, GraphQL, or gRPC patterns and document them with reusable specification templates.

use_cases.title: Review an integration contract
use_cases.description: Check an API proposal for consistency, compatibility, security coverage, usability, and documentation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a REST endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a REST endpoint for [resource] that supports [operation]. Include the path, method, request fields, response fields, status codes, and validation errors.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an API protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare REST, GraphQL, and gRPC for [service]. Consider clients, latency, streaming, schema governance, caching, and operational complexity. Recommend one approach with reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Review an API contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the provided API contract against the framework. Identify consistency, pagination, error handling, authentication, versioning, and documentation issues. Prioritize concrete changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan compatible API evolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the evolution of [current API] to support [new requirement]. Preserve compatibility, define deprecations, specify migration stages, and update contract documentation.

output_examples.input: Design a paginated endpoint for listing active users.
output: A resource-oriented endpoint using a safe retrieval method.
Cursor pagination with a bounded page size and continuation metadata.
Defined success, validation, authentication, and rate-limit responses.

output_examples.input: Choose a protocol for low-latency internal service communication with streaming.
output_examples.output: A recommendation for gRPC, supported by schema, streaming, performance, client, and operational considerations.

output_examples.input: Review an API proposal that changes a required response field.
output: A compatibility warning for existing clients.
An additive transition plan with deprecation notice and migration milestones.
Required specification, test, and documentation updates.

best_practices: Provide requirements, client types, data volume, security constraints, and compatibility expectations.
Review generated contracts with implementation owners, security reviewers, and API consumers.
Validate adapted OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents with current specification tooling.
anti_patterns: Do not treat example domains, credentials, identifiers, or schemas as production values.
Do not choose a protocol from preference alone without client and operational requirements.
Do not introduce breaking changes without versioning, deprecation, and migration planning.

faq.question: Which API styles does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers REST, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenAPI 3.1, and AsyncAPI 3.0 design patterns.

faq.question: Does this skill generate working service code?
faq.answer: No. It provides contract guidance, examples, templates, and review checklists.

faq.question: Can it help select REST, GraphQL, or gRPC?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide client, latency, streaming, caching, governance, and operational requirements for a reasoned comparison.

faq.question: Are the included URLs and data production ready?
faq.answer: No. They are illustrative placeholders and must be replaced with project-specific values.

faq.question: Does it cover API security?
faq.answer: It covers authentication, authorization, rate limiting, validation, transport security, and checklist items at a design level.

faq.question: How should teams validate the generated specification?
faq.answer: Use current OpenAPI or AsyncAPI validators, contract tests, security review, and feedback from API consumers.
